Sketcher_BSplinePolygon.doc:
The Sketcher BSplinePolygon tool shows or hides the B-spline control polygon in all sketches.

## See also

- Sketcher_CreateBSpline

Sketcher_CarbonCopy.doc:
The Sketcher CarbonCopy tool copies all geometry and constraints from another sketch into the active sketch.

Dimensional constraints which exist before the copy function remain linked to the original sketch's dimensional constraints through expressions.

Sketcher_ChangeDimensionConstraint.doc: Edits the value of a dimensional constraint.

Sketcher_Clone.doc:
The Sketcher Clone command clones the selected sketch elements from one point to another, using the last selected point as reference. If any constraints are part of the source elements, then the new constraints are linked to the source constraints; if the constraints in the source are changed, the constraints in the clone are also changed. To avoid this linking see [Sketcher Copy.

Note that a clone of a clone becomes a Sketcher Copy. If you wish to create linked constraints, clone the original source elements again.

## See also

- Sketcher_Copy
- Sketcher_Move

Sketcher_CompBSplineShowHideGeometryInfo.doc: Toggles the visibility of the information layer for all B-splines.

Sketcher_CompConstrainRadDia.doc: Constrains the radius or diameter of an arc or a circle.

Sketcher_CompCopy.doc: Creates a clone of the geometry taking as reference the last selected point.

Sketcher_CompCreateBSpline.doc: Creates a B-spline curve defined by control points.

Sketcher_CompCreateFillets.doc: Creates a fillet or chamfer between 2 lines.

Sketcher_CompCreateRegularPolygon.doc: Creates a regular polygon from a center and corner point.

Sketcher_CompExternal.doc: Creates sketch elements linked to geometry defined outside the sketch.

Sketcher_CompHorVer.doc: Constrains the selected elements either horizontally or vertically.

Sketcher_CompModifyKnotMultiplicity.doc: Modifies the multiplicity of the selected knot of a B-spline.

Sketcher_ConstrainAngle.doc:
The Sketcher ConstrainAngle tool fixes the angle between two edges (lines are then treated as infinite, and open curves are virtually extended as well), the angle of a line with the horizontal axis of the sketch, or the aperture angle of a circular arc.

## See also

- Sketcher_ConstrainPerpendicular

Sketcher_ConstrainBlock.doc:
The Sketcher ConstrainBlock tool blocks edges in place with a single constraint. It is mainly intended for B-splines, which can be difficult to fully constrain otherwise.

The block constraint only affects the freely movable parts of an edge. Blocked edges can have other constraints, and applying additional constraints to a blocked edge can modify it.

## See also

- Sketcher_ConstrainLock

Sketcher_ConstrainCoincident.doc:
The Sketcher ConstrainCoincident tool creates a coincident constraint between points, or ( ) a concentric constraint between circles, arcs and/or ellipses (by making their centers coincident). This tool is replaced by the Sketcher ConstrainCoincidentUnified tool if the Unify Coincident and PointOnObject option is selected in the preferences.

## See also

- Sketcher_ConstrainCoincidentUnified
- Sketcher_ConstrainPointOnObject

Sketcher_ConstrainCoincidentUnified.doc:
The Sketcher ConstrainCoincidentUnified tool creates a coincident constraint between points, fixes points on edges or axes (lines are then treated as infinite, and open curves are virtually extended as well), or creates a concentric constraint between circles, arcs and/or ellipses (by making their centers coincident).

This tool replaces the Sketcher ConstrainCoincident and Sketcher ConstrainPointOnObject tools if the Unify Coincident and PointOnObject option is selected in the preferences.

## See also

- Sketcher_ConstrainCoincident
- Sketcher_ConstrainPointOnObject

Sketcher_ConstrainDiameter.doc:
The Sketcher ConstrainDiameter tool fixes the diameter of circles and arcs. It cannot be used for B-spline weight circles.

## See also

- Sketcher_ConstrainRadiam
- Sketcher_ConstrainRadius

Sketcher_ConstrainDistance.doc:
The Sketcher ConstrainDistance tool fixes the length of a line, the distance between two points, the perpendicular distance between a point and a line; or, , the distance between the edges of two circles or arcs, or between the edge of a circle or arc and a line; or, , the length of an arc.

## See also

- Sketcher_ConstrainDistanceX
- Sketcher_ConstrainDistanceY

Sketcher_ConstrainDistanceX.doc:
The Sketcher ConstrainDistanceX tool fixes the horizontal distance between two points or the endpoints of a line. If a single point is pre-selected, the distance is relative to the origin of the sketch.

## See also

- Sketcher_ConstrainDistanceY
- Sketcher_ConstrainDistance

Sketcher_ConstrainDistanceY.doc:
The Sketcher ConstrainDistanceY tool fixes the vertical distance between two points or the endpoints of a line. If a single point is pre-selected, the distance is relative to the origin of the sketch.

## See also

- Sketcher_ConstrainDistanceX
- Sketcher_ConstrainDistance

Sketcher_ConstrainEqual.doc: The Sketcher ConstrainEqual tool constrains edges to have an equal length (lines) or curvature (other edges except B-splines). Selected edges must have the same type. Circles and circular arcs are of the same type (their radii are made equal), and so are ellipses and elliptical arcs (their major and minor radii are made equal).

Sketcher_ConstrainHorVer.doc:
The Sketcher ConstrainHorVer tool constrains lines or pairs of points to be horizontal (parallel to the horizontal axis of the sketch) or vertical, whichever is closest to the current alignment.

This tool combines the Sketcher ConstrainHorizontal and Sketcher ConstrainVertical tools.

## See also

- Sketcher_ConstrainHorizontal
- Sketcher_ConstrainVertical

Sketcher_ConstrainHorizontal.doc:
The Sketcher ConstrainHorizontal tool constrains lines or pairs of points to be horizontal (parallel to the horizontal axis of the sketch). In most cases it is advisable to use the combined Sketcher ConstrainHorVer tool instead.

## See also

- Sketcher_ConstrainHorVer
- Sketcher_ConstrainVertical

Sketcher_ConstrainLock.doc:
The Sketcher ConstrainLock tool applies Horizontal distance and Vertical distance constraints to points. If a single point is selected the constraints reference the origin of the sketch. If two or more points are selected the constraints reference the last point in the selection.

## See also

- Sketcher_ConstrainBlock

Sketcher_ConstrainParallel.doc: The Sketcher ConstrainParallel tool constrains lines to be parallel.

Sketcher_ConstrainPerpendicular.doc:
The Sketcher ConstrainPerpendicular tool constrains two lines to be perpendicular, or two edges, or an edge and an axis, to be perpendicular at their intersection. Lines are treated as infinite, and open curves are virtually extended as well. The constraint can also connect two edges, forcing them to be perpendicular at the joint.

## See also

- Sketcher_ConstrainAngle

Sketcher_ConstrainPointOnObject.doc:
The Sketcher ConstrainPointOnObject tool fixes points on edges or axes. Lines are treated as infinite, and open curves are virtually extended as well. This tool is replaced by the Sketcher ConstrainCoincidentUnified tool if the Unify Coincident and PointOnObject option is selected in the preferences.

## See also

- Sketcher_ConstrainCoincidentUnified
- Sketcher_ConstrainCoincident

Sketcher_ConstrainRadiam.doc:
The Sketcher ConstrainRadiam tool fixes the radius of arcs and B-spline weight circles, and the diameter of circles.

## See also

- Sketcher_ConstrainRadius
- Sketcher_ConstrainDiameter

Sketcher_ConstrainRadius.doc:
The Sketcher ConstrainRadius tool fixes the radius of circles, arcs and B-spline weight circles.

## See also

- Sketcher_ConstrainRadiam
- Sketcher_ConstrainDiameter

Sketcher_ConstrainSnellsLaw.doc: The Sketcher ConstrainSnellsLaw tool constrains two lines to follow the law of refraction of light as it penetrates through an interface where two materials with different refraction indices meet. See Snell's law.

Sketcher_ConstrainSymmetric.doc: The Sketcher ConstrainSymmetric tool constrains two points to be symmetrical around a line or axis, or around a third point.

Sketcher_ConstrainTangent.doc: The Sketcher ConstrainTangent tool constrains two edges, or an edge and an axis, to be tangent. Lines are treated as infinite, and open curves are virtually extended as well. The constraint can also connect two edges, forcing them to be tangent at the joint. If two lines are selected, or a line and the endpoint of another line, the lines are made collinear.

Sketcher_ConstrainVertical.doc:
The Sketcher ConstrainVertical tool constrains lines or pairs of points to be vertical (parallel to the vertical axis of the sketch). In most cases it is advisable to use the combined Sketcher ConstrainHorVer tool instead.

## See also

- Sketcher_ConstrainHorVer
- Sketcher_ConstrainHorizontal

Sketcher_Copy.doc:
The Sketcher Copy command copies the selected sketch elements from one point to another, using the last selected point as reference. When a copy is made, there is no link established between the copy and the original, see [Sketcher Clone.

## See also

- Sketcher_Clone
- Sketcher_Move

Sketcher_CopyClipboard.doc: Copies the selected geometries and constraints to the clipboard.

Sketcher_Create3PointArc.doc: The Sketcher Create3PointArc tool creates an arc by its endpoints and a point along the arc. This is the same tool as Sketcher CreateArc but with a different initial mode.

Sketcher_Create3PointCircle.doc:
The Sketcher Create 3PointCircle tool creates a circle by three points along the circle. This is the same tool as Sketcher CreateCircle but with a different initial mode.

## See also

- Sketcher_CreateCircle

Sketcher_CreateArc.doc:
The Sketcher CreateArc tool creates an arc by its center and its endpoints. Or optionally by its endpoints and a point along the arc.

## See also

- Sketcher_CreateCircle

Sketcher_CreateArcOfEllipse.doc:
The Sketcher CreateArcOfEllipse tool creates an arc of ellipse.

## See also

- Sketcher_CreateEllipseByCenter

Sketcher_CreateArcOfHyperbola.doc:
The Sketcher CreateArcOfHyperbola tool creates an arc of hyperbola.

## See also

- Sketcher_CreateArcOfParabola

Sketcher_CreateArcOfParabola.doc:
The Sketcher CreateArcOfParabola tool creates an arc of parabola.

## See also

- Sketcher_CreateArcOfHyperbola

Sketcher_CreateArcSlot.doc:
The Sketcher CreateArcSlot tool creates an arc slot, a closed polyline consisting of two parallel concentric arcs closed by two semicircles or two radial straight lines.

## See also

- Sketcher_CreateSlot

Sketcher_CreateBSpline.doc:
The Sketcher CreateBSpline tool creates a B-spline curve by control points. Or optionally by knot points.

## See also

- Sketcher_CreatePeriodicBSpline

Sketcher_CreateBSplineByInterpolation.doc:
The Sketcher CreateBSplineByInterpolation tool creates a B-spline curve by knot points. This is the same tool as Sketcher CreateBSpline but with a different initial mode.

## See also

- Sketcher_CreateBSpline

Sketcher_CreateChamfer.doc:
The Sketcher CreateChamfer tool creates a chamfer between two non-parallel edges. This is the same tool as Sketcher CreateFillet but with a different initial mode.

## See also

- Sketcher_CreateFillet

Sketcher_CreateCircle.doc:
The Sketcher CreateCircle tool creates a circle by its center and a point along the circle. Or optionally by three points along the circle.

## See also

- Sketcher_CreateArc

Sketcher_CreateEllipseBy3Points.doc:
The Sketcher CreateEllipseBy3Points tool creates an ellipse by the endpoints of one of its axes and a point along the ellipse. This is the same tool as Sketcher CreateEllipseByCenter but with a different initial mode.

## See also

- Sketcher_CreateEllipseByCenter

Sketcher_CreateEllipseByCenter.doc:
The Sketcher CreateEllipseByCenter tool creates an ellipse by its center, an endpoint of one of its axes, and a point along the ellipse. Or optionally by both endpoints of one of its axes and a point along the ellipse.

## See also

- Sketcher_CreateArcOfEllipse

Sketcher_CreateFillet.doc: The Sketcher CreateFillet tool creates a fillet between two non-parallel edges. The tool can also create a chamfer. If two straight edges connected by a Coincident constraint are filleted or chamfered, the corner point can optionally be preserved. The tool then adds a Point object that has a Point on object constraint with both edges. Constraints connected to the corner point are transferred to the new point object.

Sketcher_CreateHeptagon.doc:
The Sketcher CreateHeptagon tool creates a heptagon. This is the same tool as Sketcher CreateRegularPolygon but with the number of sides preset to 7.

## See also

- Sketcher_CreateRegularPolygon

Sketcher_CreateHexagon.doc:
The Sketcher CreateHexagon tool creates a hexagon. This is the same tool as Sketcher CreateRegularPolygon but with the number of sides preset to 6.

## See also

- Sketcher_CreateRegularPolygon

Sketcher_CreateLine.doc:
The Sketcher CreateLine tool creates a line. If On-View-Parameters are enabled the tool has three modes.

## See also

- Sketcher_CreatePolyline

Sketcher_CreateOblong.doc:
The Sketcher CreateOblong tool creates a rounded rectangle. This is the same tool as Sketcher CreateRectangle but with a different initial mode.

## See also

- Sketcher_CreateRectangle

Sketcher_CreateOctagon.doc:
The Sketcher CreateOctagon tool creates an octagon. This is the same tool as Sketcher CreateRegularPolygon but with the number of sides preset to 8.

## See also

- Sketcher_CreateRegularPolygon

Sketcher_CreatePentagon.doc:
The Sketcher CreatePentagon tool creates a pentagon. This is the same tool as Sketcher CreateRegularPolygon but with the number of sides preset to 5.

## See also

- Sketcher_CreateRegularPolygon

Sketcher_CreatePeriodicBSpline.doc:
The Sketcher CreatePeriodicBSpline tool creates a periodic (closed) B-spline curve by control points. This is the same tool as Sketcher CreateBSpline but with a different initial mode.

## See also

- Sketcher_CreateBSpline

Sketcher_CreatePeriodicBSplineByInterpol.doc:
The Sketcher CreatePeriodicBSplineByInterpolation tool creates a periodic (closed) B-spline curve by knot points. This is the same tool as Sketcher CreateBSpline but with a different initial mode.

## See also

- Sketcher_CreateBSpline

Sketcher_CreatePoint.doc: The Sketcher CreatePoint tool creates a point.

Sketcher_CreatePolyline.doc:
The Sketcher CreatePolyline tool creates a series of line and arc segments connected by their endpoints. The tool has several modes.

## See also

- Sketcher_CreateLine

Sketcher_CreateRectangle.doc:
The Sketcher CreateRectangle tool creates a rectangle. The tool has four modes, two of which can also produce parallelograms. Rounded corners and creating an offset copy are optional features.

## See also

- Sketcher_CreatePolyline

Sketcher_CreateRectangle_Center.doc:
The Sketcher CreateRectangle Center tool creates a centered rectangle. This is the same tool as Sketcher CreateRectangle but with a different initial mode.

## See also

- Sketcher_CreateRectangle

Sketcher_CreateRegularPolygon.doc: The Sketcher CreateRegularPolygon tool creates a regular polygon.

Sketcher_CreateSlot.doc:
The Sketcher CreateSlot tool creates a slot, a closed polyline consisting of two semicircles connected by two parallel straight lines.

## See also

- Sketcher_CreateArcSlot

Sketcher_CreateSquare.doc:
The Sketcher CreateSquare tool creates a square. This is the same tool as Sketcher CreateRegularPolygon but with the number of sides preset to 4.

## See also

- Sketcher_CreateRegularPolygon

Sketcher_CreateTriangle.doc:
The Sketcher CreateTriangle tool creates an equilateral triangle. This is the same tool as Sketcher CreateRegularPolygon but with the number of sides preset to 3.

## See also

- Sketcher_CreateRegularPolygon

Sketcher_Cut.doc: Cuts the selected geometries and constraints to the clipboard.

Sketcher_DeleteAllConstraints.doc:
The Sketcher DeleteAllConstraints tool deletes all constraints from the sketch.

## See also

- Sketcher_DeleteAllGeometry

Sketcher_DeleteAllGeometry.doc:
The Sketcher DeleteAllGeometry tool deletes all geometry and all constraints from the sketch.

## See also

- Sketcher_DeleteAllConstraints

Sketcher_Dimension.doc: The Sketcher Dimension tool is the context-sensitive constraint tool of the Sketcher Workbench. Based on the current selection, it offers appropriate dimensional constraints, but also geometric constraints.

Sketcher_EditSketch.doc:
The Sketcher EditSketch tool opens the Sketcher Dialog to edit an existing sketch.

## See also

- Sketcher_LeaveSketch

Sketcher_Extend.doc:
The Sketcher Extend tool extends or shortens a line or an arc to an arbitrary location, or to a target edge or point.

## See also

- Sketcher_Trimming

Sketcher_Grid.doc:
The Sketcher Grid tool toggles the grid in the sketch currently being edited. Settings can be changed in the related menu.

## See also

- Sketcher_Snap

Sketcher_Intersection.doc:
The Sketcher Intersection tool intersects faces and/or edges belonging to objects outside the sketch with the sketch plane. The intersected geometry is called "external geometry". It stays parametrically linked to its source objects. External geometry is marked with a dedicated color (default magenta) and linetype. It can be defining geometry that is visible outside the sketch or construction geometry that is not visible outside the sketch.

## See also

- Sketcher_ToggleConstruction

Sketcher_JoinCurves.doc: The Sketcher JoinCurves tool creates a B-spline by joining two existing B-splines or other edges.

Sketcher_LeaveSketch.doc:
The Sketcher LeaveSketch tool finishes sketch edit mode and closes the Sketcher Dialog.

## See also

- Sketcher_EditSketch

Sketcher_MapSketch.doc:
The Sketcher MapSketch tool attaches a sketch to selected geometry.

Typical use cases are:

- The sketch was created on a standard plane (XY, XZ or YZ) and you want to attach it to the face of a solid in order to build a new feature upon it.
- The sketch was attached to a specific face of a solid but you need to attached it to a different face.
- A broken model needs to be repaired.

## See also

- Sketcher_ReorientSketch
- Sketcher_NewSketch

Sketcher_MergeSketches.doc: The Sketcher MergeSketches tool merges two or more sketches.

Sketcher_MirrorSketch.doc: The Sketcher MirrorSketch tool mirrors sketches across their X axis, Y axis, or origin.

Sketcher_Move.doc:
The Sketcher Move command moves the selected sketch elements from one point to another, using the last selected point as reference.

## See also

- Sketcher_Clone
- Sketcher_Copy

Sketcher_NewSketch.doc:
The Sketcher NewSketch tool creates a new sketch and opens the Sketcher Dialog to edit it.

Note that the PartDesign Workbench has its own new sketch tool. When working on a PartDesign Body that tool should be used instead.

## See also

- PartDesign_NewSketch
- Sketcher_MapSketch
- Sketcher_ReorientSketch

Sketcher_Offset.doc: The Sketcher Offset tool creates equidistant edges around selected edges.

Sketcher_Paste.doc: Pastes the geometries and constraints from the clipboard into the sketch.

Sketcher_ProfilesHexagon1.doc: Creates a hexagonal profile in the sketch.

Sketcher_Projection.doc:
The Sketcher Projection tool projects edges and/or vertices belonging to objects outside the sketch onto the sketch plane. The projected geometry is called "external geometry". It stays parametrically linked to its source objects. External geometry is marked with a dedicated color (default magenta) and linetype. It can be defining geometry that is visible outside the sketch or construction geometry that is not visible outside the sketch.

## See also

- Sketcher_ToggleConstruction

Sketcher_RectangularArray.doc: The Sketcher Rectangular array command creates an array of selected sketcher elements.

Sketcher_RemoveAxesAlignment.doc: The Sketcher RemoveAxesAlignment tool removes the axes alignment of selected edges by replacing Horizontal and Vertical constraints with Parallel and Perpendicular constraints. The edges can then be rotated without losing their orthogonal relationship.

Sketcher_RenderingOrder.doc:
The Sketcher RenderingOrder tool itself currently does not do anything. But in the related menu the rendering order of all sketches can be changed.

In case of coincident objects, the rendering order determines which elements appear on top, and are therefore selected first, in the 3D view.

Sketcher_ReorientSketch.doc:
The Sketcher ReorientSketch tool places a sketch on one of the main planes with an optional offset. It can also be used to detach a sketch.

## See also

- Sketcher_MapSketch
- Sketcher_NewSketch

Sketcher_RestoreInternalAlignmentGeometr.doc: The Sketcher RestoreInternalAlignmentGeometry tool deletes the internal geometry of elements, or recreates missing internal geometry. The tool does not delete internal geometry that has associated constraints.

Sketcher_Rotate.doc: The Sketcher Rotate tool rotates or optionally creates rotated copies of selected elements. Copies are evenly distributed along the rotation angle.

Sketcher_Scale.doc: The Sketcher Scale tool scales or optionally creates scaled copies of selected elements.

Sketcher_SelectConflictingConstraints.doc:
The Sketcher SelectConflictingConstraints tool selects the conflicting constraints in the sketch.

If such constraints exist in a sketch the Solver messages section of the Sketcher Dialog displays this message:

- Over-constrained: (#, #, #)

Where *(#, #, #)* are the indices of the constraints. Clicking the underlined text will select the conflicting constraints.

Sketcher_SelectConstraints.doc: The Sketcher SelectConstraints tool selects the constraints associated with sketch elements.

Sketcher_SelectElementsAssociatedWithCon.doc: The Sketcher SelectElementsAssociatedWithConstraints tool selects the sketch elements associated with constraints.

Sketcher_SelectElementsWithDoFs.doc:
The Sketcher SelectElementsWithDoFs tool selects the not fully constrained elements in the sketch.

If such elements exist in a sketch the Solver messages section of the Sketcher Dialog displays this message:

- Under constrained: n DoF(s)

Where *n* is the remaining number of degrees of freedom. Clicking the underlined text will select the under-constrained elements.

Please note that a sketch can also have redundant constraints if one of the other solver messages is displayed.

Sketcher_SelectHorizontalAxis.doc: The Sketcher SelectHorizontalAxis tool selects the horizontal axis of the sketch.

Sketcher_SelectOrigin.doc: The Sketcher SelectOrigin tool selects the origin of the sketch.

Sketcher_SelectRedundantConstraints.doc:
The Sketcher SelectRedundantConstraints tool selects the redundant constraints in the sketch.

If such constraints exist in a sketch the Solver messages section of the Sketcher Dialog displays this message:

- Redundant constraints: (#, #, #)

Where *(#, #, #)* are the indices of the constraints. Clicking the underlined text will select the redundant constraints.

Please note that a sketch can also have redundant constraints if one of the other solver messages is displayed.

Sketcher_SelectVerticalAxis.doc: The Sketcher SelectVerticalAxis tool selects the vertical axis of the sketch.

Sketcher_Snap.doc:
The Sketcher Snap tool toggles snapping in all sketches. Individual snaps and settings can be changed in the related menu.

Snapping only works while creating geometry. Note that snapping is just a drawing aid, it does not produce additional constraints.

## See also

- Sketcher_Grid

Sketcher_Split.doc:
The Sketcher Split tool splits an edge. If the edge is a closed curve (i.e. a circle, an ellipse or a periodic B-spline) it is converted to an open curve (an arc, an arc of ellipse or a non-periodic B-spline respectively).

## See also

- Sketcher_Trimming

Sketcher_StopOperation.doc: The Sketcher StopOperation tool stops any currently running Sketcher tool.

Sketcher_SwitchVirtualSpace.doc:
The Sketcher SwitchVirtualSpace tool either (un)hides constraints or switches the visible virtual space.

A sketch has two virtual spaces that can contain constraints. All constraints are created in the main virtual space, but they can be hidden which moves them to the other virtual space.

Sketcher_Symmetry.doc:
The Sketcher Symmetry creates mirrored copies of selected elements.

## See also

- Sketcher_MirrorSketch

Sketcher_ToggleActiveConstraint.doc:
The Sketcher ToggleActiveConstraint tool activates or deactivates selected constraints. Deactivating constraints allows you to test other geometry arrangements without deleting constraints.

This is tool is similar to Sketcher ToggleDrivingConstraint, but contrary to that tool also works for geometric constraints, and values of deactivated dimensional constraints are preserved.

## See also

- Sketcher_ToggleDrivingConstraint

Sketcher_ToggleConstruction.doc:
The Sketcher ToggleConstruction tool either toggles the geometry creation tools to/from construction mode, or toggles selected geometry to/from construction geometry.

Construction geometry is marked with a dedicated color (default blue) and ( ) linetype. Construction geometry is not visible outside the sketch, it is intended to help define constraints and other geometry inside the sketch itself. Construction lines can however be used as a rotation axis by PartDesign Revolution.

Sketcher_ToggleDrivingConstraint.doc:
The Sketcher ToggleDrivingConstraint tool either toggles the dimensional constraint creation tools between driving and reference mode, or toggles selected dimensional constraints between those modes.

Contrary to driving constraints, reference constraints do not constrain the sketch, their value depends on other constraints, they are driven. They can be useful to verify measurements. They can be used in expressions, but not in the sketch itself.

## See also

- Sketcher_ToggleActiveConstraint

Sketcher_Translate.doc: The Sketcher Translate tool moves or optionally creates copies of selected elements. Copies are evenly distributes along one or two directions.

Sketcher_Trimming.doc:
The Sketcher Trimming tool trims an edge at the nearest intersections with other edges. If the selected edge does not intersect other edges it will be deleted.

## See also

- Sketcher_Split
- Sketcher_Extend

Sketcher_ValidateSketch.doc:
The Sketcher ValidateSketch tool can analyze and repair a sketch that is no longer editable or has invalid constraints, or add missing coincident constraints to a sketch created from imported geometry such as DXF files. It can also be useful to locate a missing coincidence in a native sketch that generates an error when trying to apply a PartDesign feature.

## See also

- Sketcher_ConstrainCoincident

Sketcher_ViewSection.doc: The Sketcher ViewSection tool toggles a temporary section plane that hides any objects and parts of objects in front of the sketch plane while the sketch is in edit mode. This is a per-sketch setting stored in the Section View property of sketches.

Sketcher_ViewSketch.doc: The Sketcher ViewSketch tool aligns the 3D view with the sketch. The view is rotated so that the view direction is perpendicular to the sketch plane, and the X axis of the sketch appears horizontal. It is useful if you have changed the view orientation to examine another aspect of the model and want to return to the default sketch view.

Spreadsheet_AlignBottom.doc: The Spreadsheet AlignBottom tool aligns the contents of selected cells to the bottom.

Spreadsheet_AlignCenter.doc: The Spreadsheet AlignCenter tool aligns the contents of selected cells to the center horizontally.

Spreadsheet_AlignLeft.doc: The Spreadsheet AlignLeft tool aligns the contents of selected cells to the left.

Spreadsheet_AlignRight.doc: The Spreadsheet AlignRight tool aligns the contents of selected cells to the right.

Spreadsheet_AlignTop.doc: The Spreadsheet AlignTop tool aligns the contents of selected cells to the top.

Spreadsheet_AlignVCenter.doc: The Spreadsheet AlignVCenter tool aligns the contents of selected cells to the center vertically.

Spreadsheet_CreateSheet.doc: The Spreadsheet CreateSheet tool adds a new spreadsheet to the active document.

Spreadsheet_Export.doc:
The Spreadsheet Export tool exports a spreadsheet as a CSV file, which can be used in other applications. Note that the character, and not the , is the default field delimiter. But this can be changed in the Spreadsheet Preferences ( ).

## See also

- Spreadsheet_Import

Spreadsheet_Import.doc:
The Spreadsheet Import tool imports a CSV file into a new spreadsheet. Note that the character, and not the , is the default field delimiter. But this can be changed in the Spreadsheet Preferences ( ).

## See also

- Spreadsheet_Export

Spreadsheet_MergeCells.doc: The Spreadsheet MergeCells tool merges a rectangular cell range.

Spreadsheet_SetAlias.doc: The Spreadsheet SetAlias tool opens a dialog to set up an alias for a cell. Instead of using the exact cell name like A2, B3, or C4, a custom name can be used.

Spreadsheet_SplitCell.doc: The Spreadsheet SplitCell tool splits a previously merged cell.

Spreadsheet_StyleBold.doc: The Spreadsheet StyleBold tool toggles the contents of selected cells to/from bold.

Spreadsheet_StyleItalic.doc: The Spreadsheet StyleItalic tool toggles the contents of selected cells to/from italic.

Spreadsheet_StyleUnderline.doc: The Spreadsheet StyleUnderline tool toggles the contents of selected cells to/from underlined.

Std_About.doc:
The Std About command opens a dialog box that shows information about the FreeCAD program.

ATTENTION: Do not take a screenshot of this dialog box! Instead press the Copy to clipboard button and then paste the information in your help request.

The Std ActivateNextWindow command activates the next window in the Main view area. The next window is determined by the tabs order in Main view area.

Std_ActivatePrevWindow.doc:

- Std_Windows

Std_AddonMgr.doc:
The Std AddonMgr command opens the Addon manager. With the Addon manager you can install and manage external workbenches, macros, and preference packs provided by the FreeCAD community. By default the available addons are taken from two repositories, FreeCAD-addons and from the Macros recipes page. If GitPython and git are installed on your system, additional macros will be loaded from FreeCAD-macros. Custom repositories can be added in the Addon manager preferences.

Due to changes to the GitHub platform in the year 2020 the Addon manager no longer works if you use FreeCAD version 0.17 or earlier. You need to upgrade to version 0.18.5 or later. Alternatively you can install addons manually, see Notes below.

- External_workbenches

Std_AlignToSelection.doc: The Std AlignToSelection command points the camera in the active 3D view in the opposite direction of the normal of a planar face, or the opposite direction of a straight edge.

Std_Alignment.doc:
The Std Alignment command aligns an object in relation to a fixed reference object using one or more point pairs.

## See also

Std_AxisCross.doc:
The Std AxisCross command toggles the axis cross in the active 3D view.

The axis cross consists of three arrows representing the positive X, Y and Z axis of the global coordinate system. Their common start point is the origin of the global coordinate system.

Std_BoxElementSelection.doc:
The Std BoxElementSelection command selects faces from a user defined rectangular area, a box, in the 3D view.

Note that if a whole object falls inside the rectangle, the object itself, instead of its faces, is selected. To avoid this create two box selections for each object (hold down Ctrl while dragging the 2nd rectangle), or use the Part BoxSelection command instead.

## See also

Std_BoxSelection.doc:
The Std BoxSelection command selects objects from a user defined rectangular area, a box, in the 3D view.

## See also

Std_CascadeWindows.doc:
The Std CascadeWindows command rearranges the windows in the Main view area so that they are all visible but do overlap. The result is determined by the order in which the windows were last activated.

Std_ClarifySelection.doc: Displays a context menu at the mouse cursor to select overlapping or obstructed geometry in the 3D view.

Std_CloseAllWindows.doc:
The Std CloseAllWindows command closes all windows, thereby closing all documents.

## See also

The Std Copy command copies objects to the Clipboard.

Std_Cut.doc:
The Std Cut command is limited: it can only be used for spreadsheet cells. The command copies the contents and properties of cells to the Clipboard and then clears them.

To cut other objects you can use the Std Copy command followed by a delete operation.

## See also

- Std_DuplicateSelection

Std_Delete.doc: The Std Delete command deletes selected objects.

Std_DemoMode.doc: The Std DemoMode command will continuously rotate the camera in a 3D view.

Std_DependencyGraph.doc:
The Std DependencyGraph command displays the dependencies between objects in the active document in a graph. As opposed to the Tree view, objects are listed in reverse chronological order, with the first created object at the bottom.

It can be useful in analyzing a FreeCAD document and locating forks in a tree. The dependency graph layout will depend on which workbench was used to create the objects in the document. For example a model made exclusively in the PartDesign workbench can display a linear dependency graph with a single vertical branch. A model made with Part operations will have many branches, but for a single part they will join up at the top after Boolean operations. If they don't, it means that they are separate objects.

The dependency graph is purely a visualization tool, therefore it cannot be edited. It automatically updates if changes are made to the model.

## See also

The Std DlgParameter command opens the Parameter Editor. In the Parameter Editor the parameters that control the behavior of FreeCAD and its workbenches can be inspected and optionally removed, added or changed. The parameters are stored in a file called user.cfg, the location of this file depends on your OS.

Working with the Parameter Editor requires some experience. For the most common parameters the Preferences Editor should be used instead.

FreeCAD can store camera settings in up to 50 'frozen views'. The menu options that deal with frozen views can be found in the View → Freeze display submenu. Std_LinkImport.doc:
[Std LinkImport

imports the Linked Object from a Link into the current document, and then changes the attachment to this object.

This operation is helpful when working with assemblies in order to organize re-usable models that may be located in other documents.

Use [Std LinkImportAll to import all linked objects.

## See also

Std_LinkImportAll.doc:
[Std LinkImportAll

imports all Linked Objects from Links into the current document, and then changes the attachment to point to these imported objects.

This command essentially runs [Std LinkImport for all Links in a document.

Std_LinkMake.doc:
[Std LinkMake

creates an App Link (`App::Link` class), a type of object that references or links to another object in the same document, or in another document. It is especially designed to efficiently duplicate a single object multiple times, which helps with the creation of complex assemblies from smaller subassemblies, and from multiple reusable components like screws, nuts, and similar fasteners.

The App Link object was newly introduced in v0.19; in the past, simple duplication of objects could be achieved with [Draft Clone, but this is a less efficient solution due to its implementation, which essentially creates a copy of the internal Shape of the source object. Instead, a Link directly references the original Shape, so it is more memory-efficient.

By itself the Link object can behave like an array, duplicating its base object many times; this can be done by setting its Element Count property to or larger. This "Link Array" object can also be created with the different array tools of the Draft Workbench, for example, [Draft OrthoArray, [Draft PolarArray, and [Draft CircularArray.

When used with the PartDesign Workbench, Links are intended to be used with [PartDesign Bodies, so it is recommended to set Display Mode Body to to select the features of the entire Body, and not the individual features. To create arrays of the internal PartDesign Features, use [PartDesign LinearPattern, [PartDesign PolarPattern, and [PartDesign MultiTransform.

The [Std LinkMake tool is not defined by a particular workbench, but by the base system, thus it is found in the structure toolbar that is available in all workbenches. The Link object, used in conjunction with [Std Part to group various objects, forms the basis of the Assembly3 and Assembly4 Workbenches.

## See also

- Std_Part
- Std_Group
- PartDesign_Body

Std_LinkMakeRelative.doc:
[Std LinkMakeRelative

creates an App Link (`App::Link` class), just like [Std LinkMake, but it operates on selected subelements first, and sets the Link Transform to `True`.

Std_LinkReplace.doc:
[Std LinkReplace

replaces an object that is inside another for an App Link version of the former.

This operation acts on the "children" of a "parent" object as seen in the tree view. For example, given two objects (A and B) that participate in a [Part Boolean operation, say, C = A + B, the A object can be replaced by a Link, so that C = A_link + B.

This operation can be done to replace nested objects that are in a complex assembly for a Link, which may be more efficient if that nested object is used many times in different sub-assemblies. The inverse operation is [Std LinkUnlink. To create a generic Link see [Std LinkMake.

## See also

- Std_LinkMake
- Std_LinkMakeRelative
- Std_LinkUnlink

Std_LinkSelectAllLinks.doc:
The Std LinkSelectAllLinks command selects all App Link objects, links, that directly or indirectly link to the same source object.

- Std_LinkSelectLinkedFinal

Std_LinkSelectLinked.doc:
The Std LinkSelectLinked command selects the Linked Object, the source object, of an App Link object, a link.

- Std_LinkSelectAllLinks

Std_LinkSelectLinkedFinal.doc:
The Std LinkSelectLinkedFinal command selects the Linked Object, the source object, of an App Link object, a link. But if that source object is also a link its linked object is selected instead. This is repeated until the linked object is not a link. This final source object is the deepest linked object.

This operation is used to remove a Link from a container like [Std Part, and instead place the real object inside.

Std_Part.doc:
[Std Part

(internally called App Part) is a general purpose container that keeps together a group of objects so that they can be moved together as a unit in the 3D view.

The Std Part element was developed to be the basic building block to create mechanical assemblies. In particular, it is meant to arrange objects that have a Part TopoShape, like Part Primitives, PartDesign Bodies, and other Part Features. The Std Part provides an Origin object with local X, Y, and Z axes, and standard planes, that can be used as reference to position the contained objects. In addition, Std Parts may be nested inside other Std Parts to create a big assembly from smaller sub-assemblies.

Although it is primarily intended for solid bodies, the Std Part can be used to manage any object that has a Placement property, so it can also contain Mesh Features, sketches, and other objects derived from the App GeoFeature class.

Do not confuse the [PartDesign Body with the [Std Part. The first one is a specific object used in the PartDesign Workbench, intended to model a single contiguous solid by means of PartDesign Features. On the other hand, the Std Part is not used for modelling, just to arrange different objects in space, with the intention to create assemblies.

The [Std Part tool is not defined by a particular workbench, but by the base system, thus it is found in the structure toolbar that is available in all workbenches. To group objects arbitrarily without considering their position, use [Std Group; this object does not affect the placements of the elements that it contains, it is essentially just a folder that is used to keep the Tree view organized.

Std_SendToPythonConsole.doc:
The Std SendToPythonConsole command creates variables in the Python console referencing a selected object and its selected subshapes, along with some other useful references. The variables and the code involved can be used in the development of Python code.

Depending on the selected object and its selected subshapes, if any, the following variables are created:

+++ | Variable name | Referenced object(s) | +=================+=========================================================================================================================================================+ | | The document containing the selected object | | | | | | | +++ | | The selected Link object (only created if the selected object is a Link) | | | | | | | +++ | | Depending on the selected object: | | | The selected object itself (if the selected object is not a Link) | | | The Linked object (if the selected object is a Link) | +++ | | Depending on the type of | | | The property of (for objects derived from the class) | | | The property of (for Mesh objects) | | | The property of (for Points objects) | +++ | | The first selected subshape (only created if at least one subshape is selected) | | | | | | | +++ | | A list containing all subshapes (only created if two or more subshapes are selected) | | | | | | | +++

>>> ### Begin command Std_SendToPythonConsole >>> try: >>> del(doc,lnk,obj,shp,sub,subs) >>> except Exception: >>> pass >>> >>> doc = App.getDocument("Unnamed") >>> lnk = doc.getObject("Link") >>> obj = lnk.getLinkedObject() >>> shp = obj.Shape >>> sub = obj.getSubObject("Edge10") >>> subs = [obj.getSubObject("Edge10"),obj.getSubObject("Face3"),obj.getSubObject("Vertex5"),] >>> ### End command Std_SendToPythonConsole

If the object is not a Mesh, but a parametric Shape or surface, it must be converted first to a mesh using [Mesh FromPartShape.

creates a surface from a series of connected boundary edges. The curvature of the surface can be additionally controlled by non-boundary edges and vertices, and a support surface.

The base geometry can belong to curves created with the Draft Workbench or the Sketcher Workbench, but can also belong to solid objects such as those created with the Part Workbench or the PartDesign Workbench.

Surface_GeomFillSurface.doc:
[Surface GeomFillSurface

creates a parametric surface from two, three, or four boundary edges, trying to create a smooth transition between them.

Surface_Sections.doc:
[Surface Sections

is used to create a surface from edges that represent transversal sections of a surface.

TechDraw_2LineCenterLine.doc:
The TechDraw 2LineCenterLine tool adds a centerline between two edges.

## See also

- TechDraw_FaceCenterLine
- TechDraw_2PointCenterLine

TechDraw_2PointCenterLine.doc:
The TechDraw 2PointCenterLine tool adds a centerline between two points.

## See also

- TechDraw_FaceCenterLine
- TechDraw_2LineCenterLine

TechDraw_2PointCosmeticLine.doc:
The TechDraw 2PointCosmeticLine tool adds a cosmetic line between two points. The points can be 2D or 3D. The resulting line can be used for dimensioning.

## See also

- TechDraw_FaceCenterLine
- TechDraw_2LineCenterLine
- TechDraw_2PointCenterLine

TechDraw_3PtAngleDimension.doc:
The TechDraw 3PtAngleDimension tool adds an angular dimension to a View. The dimension shows the interior angle between three points.

## See also

- TechDraw_AngleDimension

TechDraw_ActiveView.doc:
The TechDraw ActiveView tool inserts a bitmap image of the active 3D window into a drawing page.

## See also

- TechDraw_Image

TechDraw_AlignVertexesHorizontally.doc: Aligns the selected vertices or edges horizontally to the view rotation.

TechDraw_AlignVertexesVertically.doc: Aligns the selected vertices or edges vertically to the view rotation.

TechDraw_AngleDimension.doc:
The TechDraw AngleDimension tool adds an angular dimension to a View. The dimension shows the interior angle between two straight edges.

## See also

- TechDraw_3PtAngleDimension

TechDraw_Annotation.doc:
The TechDraw Annotation tool adds a text block to a drawing page.

## See also

- TechDraw_RichTextAnnotation

TechDraw_ArchView.doc:
The TechDraw ArchView tool inserts an Arch View, a view of an Arch SectionPlane, on a TechDraw page. The TechDraw View tool can also create an Arch View.

## See also

- Arch_SectionPlane

TechDraw_AreaDimension.doc:
The TechDraw AreaDimension tool adds an area dimension to a face in a Part View.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionAreaAnnotation

TechDraw_AxoLengthDimension.doc: The TechDraw AxoLengthDimension tool adds a length dimension to an axonometric view. The dimension may be the length of an edge or the distance between two points.

TechDraw_Balloon.doc:
The TechDraw Balloon tool can add balloons with leader line in a drawing.

## See also

- TechDraw_Annotation

TechDraw_BrokenView.doc:
The TechDraw BrokenView tool inserts a "broken view" that is either based on an existing part view, or one or more objects, such as Bodies or Parts. The broken view also requires one or more sketches that define the location and size of the areas to be removed. The BrokenView behaves similarly to other Views. The projection direction is taken from the existing part view, the 3D camera direction or the normal of a selected face.

## See also

- TechDraw_View

TechDraw_CenterLineGroup.doc: Inserts a centerline to a face, or between 2 lines or edges.

TechDraw_ClipGroup.doc: The TechDraw ClipGroup tool creates a clipping window which can contain Views.

TechDraw_ClipGroupAdd.doc: The TechDraw ClipGroupAdd tool adds a View to an existing Clip.

TechDraw_ClipGroupRemove.doc: The TechDraw ClipGroupRemove tool removes a View from an existing Clip and returns it to the Page area.

TechDraw_CommandAddOffsetVertex.doc: The TechDraw CommandAddOffsetVertex tool adds a cosmetic vertex at a specified offset from a selected vertex.

TechDraw_CommandVertexCreationGroup.doc: Adds cosmetic vertices at the intersectionss of selected edges.

TechDraw_ComplexSection.doc:
The TechDraw ComplexSection tool inserts a cross-section view based on an existing part view and a profile.

## See also

- TechDraw_SectionView
- TechDraw_View

TechDraw_CosmeticCircle.doc:
The TechDraw CosmeticCircle tool adds a cosmetic circle at a selected center point. The point can be 2D or 3D.

## See also

- TechDraw_2PointCosmeticLine

TechDraw_CosmeticEraser.doc: The TechDraw CosmeticEraser tool removes cosmetic objects. Cosmetic objects include cosmetic vertices, cosmetic lines and centerlines.

TechDraw_CosmeticVertex.doc:
The TechDraw CosmeticVertex tool adds a vertex, which is not part of the source geometry, to a view. This vertex behaves like any other vertex and can be used for dimensioning.

## See also

- TechDraw_Midpoints
- TechDraw_Quadrants

TechDraw_DecorateLine.doc:
The TechDraw DecorateLine tool changes the appearance of edges, including cosmetic lines and centerlines. It can also make edges invisible.

## See also

- TechDraw_ShowAll

TechDraw_DetailView.doc:
The TechDraw DetailView tool creates a view of a small area of an existing view.

## See also

- TechDraw_View

TechDraw_DiameterDimension.doc:
The TechDraw DiameterDimension tool adds a diameter dimension to a View. The dimension may be applied to any edge which is a circle or circular arc.

For more information see TechDraw RadiusDimension.

## See also

- TechDraw_RadiusDimension

TechDraw_Dimension.doc: The TechDraw Dimension tool is the TechDraw equivalent of the Sketcher Dimension tool. It offers contextual dimensioning and thus can replace most of the other dimension tools.

TechDraw_DimensionRepair.doc:
The TechDraw DimensionRepair tool can adjust the 2D or 3D geometry references of a dimension. These references may become incorrect due to the "topological naming problem" or Hidden Line Removal.

See TechDraw LengthDimension for more on dimensions and the topological naming problem.

## See also

- TechDraw_LengthDimension

TechDraw_DraftView.doc:
The TechDraw DraftView tool inserts a view of a selected Part-based or Group object into a drawing page. Unlike the standard View tool, views created with this tool are handled by the Draft Workbench, and specially designed for showing 2D objects. See Notes.

## See also

- TechDraw_ArchView

TechDraw_ExportPageDXF.doc:
The TechDraw ExportPageDXF tool saves a drawing page as a DXF file.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExportPageSVG
- Draft_DXF

TechDraw_ExportPageSVG.doc:
The TechDraw ExportPageSVG tool saves the current drawing page as an SVG file.

## See also

- TechDraw_Templates
- Draft_SVG

TechDraw_ExtensionArcLengthAnnotation.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionArcLengthAnnotation tool calculates the arc length of selected edges and inserts an arc length annotation.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionCreateLengthArc

TechDraw_ExtensionAreaAnnotation.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionAreaAnnotation tool calculates the area of selected faces and inserts an area annotation.

## See also

- TechDraw_AreaDimension

TechDraw_ExtensionCascadeDimensionGroup.doc: Evenly spaces the selected horizontal dimensions:- Specify the cascade spacing (optional)- Select two or more horizontal dimensions- The first dimension defines the position- Click this tool.

TechDraw_ExtensionCascadeHorizDimension.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionCascadeHorizDimension tool evenly spaces horizontal dimensions.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionCascadeVertDimension
- TechDraw_ExtensionCascadeObliqueDimension

TechDraw_ExtensionCascadeObliqueDimensio.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionCascadeObliqueDimension tool evenly spaces oblique dimensions.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionCascadeHorizDimension
- TechDraw_ExtensionCascadeVertDimension

TechDraw_ExtensionCascadeVertDimension.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionCascadeVertDimension tool evenly spaces vertical dimensions.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionCascadeHorizDimension
- TechDraw_ExtensionCascadeObliqueDimension

TechDraw_ExtensionChamferDimensionGroup.doc: Inserts a horizontal size and angle dimension for a chamfer from 2 selected vertices.

TechDraw_ExtensionChangeLineAttributes.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionChangeLineAttributes tool changes the attributes (style, width and color) of cosmetic lines and centerlines.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionSelectLineAttributes

TechDraw_ExtensionCircleCenterLines.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionCircleCenterLines tool adds centerlines to circles and arcs.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionHoleCircle

TechDraw_ExtensionCircleCenterLinesGroup.doc: Adds centerlines to selected circles and arcs.

TechDraw_ExtensionCreateChainDimensionGr.doc: Inserts a sequence of aligned horizontal dimensions to at least three selected vertices, where the first two define the direction.

TechDraw_ExtensionCreateCoordDimensionGr.doc: Adds evenly spaced horizontal dimensions between 3 or more vertices aligned to a shared baseline.

TechDraw_ExtensionCreateHorizChainDimens.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionCreateHorizChainDimension tool creates horizontal chain dimensions: a sequence of aligned dimensions.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionCreateVertChainDimension
- TechDraw_ExtensionCreateObliqueChainDimension

TechDraw_ExtensionCreateHorizChamferDime.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionCreateHorizChamferDimension tool creates a horizontal size and angle dimension for a chamfer.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionCreateVertChamferDimension

TechDraw_ExtensionCreateHorizCoordDimens.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionCreateHorizCoordDimension tool creates horizontal coordinate dimensions: multiple evenly spaced dimensions starting from the same baseline.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionCreateVertCoordDimension
- TechDraw_ExtensionCreateObliqueCoordDimension

TechDraw_ExtensionCreateLengthArc.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionCreateLengthArc tool creates an arc length dimension.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionArcLengthAnnotation

TechDraw_ExtensionCreateObliqueChainDime.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionCreateObliqueChainDimension tool creates oblique chain dimensions: a sequence of aligned dimensions.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionCreateHorizChainDimension
- TechDraw_ExtensionCreateVertChainDimension

TechDraw_ExtensionCreateObliqueCoordDime.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionCreateObliqueCoordDimension tool creates oblique coordinate dimensions: multiple evenly spaced dimensions starting from the same baseline.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionCreateHorizCoordDimension
- TechDraw_ExtensionCreateVertCoordDimension

TechDraw_ExtensionCreateVertChainDimensi.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionCreateVertChainDimension tool creates vertical chain dimensions: a sequence of aligned dimensions.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionCreateHorizChainDimension
- TechDraw_ExtensionCreateObliqueChainDimension

TechDraw_ExtensionCreateVertChamferDimen.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionCreateVertChamferDimension tool creates a vertical size and angle dimension for a chamfer.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionCreateHorizChamferDimension

TechDraw_ExtensionCreateVertCoordDimensi.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionCreateVertCoordDimension tool creates vertical coordinate dimensions: multiple evenly spaced dimensions starting from the same baseline.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionCreateHorizCoordDimension
- TechDraw_ExtensionCreateObliqueCoordDimension

TechDraw_ExtensionCustomizeFormat.doc: The TechDraw ExtensionCustomizeFormat tool customizes the formatting of a balloon text or dimension text. GD&T symbols and other special characters can be added.

TechDraw_ExtensionDecreaseDecimal.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionDecreaseDecimal tool decreases the number of decimal places of the dimension text.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionIncreaseDecimal

TechDraw_ExtensionDrawCirclesGroup.doc: Adds a cosmetic circle based on two vertices, where the first selection is the centerpoint and the second is the radius.

TechDraw_ExtensionDrawCosmArc.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionDrawCosmArc tool adds a cosmetic counter clockwise arc based on three vertexes.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionDrawCosmCircle

TechDraw_ExtensionDrawCosmCircle.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionDrawCosmCircle tool adds a cosmetic circle based on two vertexes.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionDrawCosmArc

TechDraw_ExtensionDrawCosmCircle3Points.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionDrawCosmCircle3Points tool adds a cosmetic circle based on three vertexes.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionDrawCosmArc

TechDraw_ExtensionExtendLine.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionExtendLine tool extends a cosmetic line or centerline at both ends.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionShortenLine

TechDraw_ExtensionExtendShortenLineGroup.doc: Extends a selected cosmetic line or centerline at both ends by the specified delta distance.

TechDraw_ExtensionHoleCircle.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionHoleCircle tool adds centerlines to a circular pattern of circles.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionCircleCenterLines

TechDraw_ExtensionIncreaseDecimal.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionIncreaseDecimal tool increases the number of decimal places of the dimension text.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionDecreaseDecimal

TechDraw_ExtensionIncreaseDecreaseGroup.doc: Increases the number of decimal places of the dimension.

TechDraw_ExtensionInsertDiameter.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionInsertDiameter tool inserts a '⌀' symbol at the beginning of the dimension text.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionInsertSquare
- TechDraw_ExtensionInsertRepetition

TechDraw_ExtensionInsertPrefixGroup.doc: Inserts a '⌀' symbol at the beginning of the dimension text.

TechDraw_ExtensionInsertRepetition.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionInsertRepetition tool inserts a repeated feature count at the beginning of the dimension text.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionInsertDiameter
- TechDraw_ExtensionInsertSquare

TechDraw_ExtensionInsertSquare.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionInsertSquare tool inserts a '□' symbol at the beginning of the dimension text.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionInsertDiameter
- TechDraw_ExtensionInsertRepetition

TechDraw_ExtensionLinePPGroup.doc: Adds a cosmetic line parallel to the selected line through the selected vertex.

TechDraw_ExtensionLineParallel.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionLineParallel tool adds a cosmetic line parallel to another line through a vertex.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionLinePerpendicular

TechDraw_ExtensionLinePerpendicular.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionLinePerpendicular tool adds a cosmetic line perpendicular to another line through a vertex.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionLineParallel

TechDraw_ExtensionLockUnlockView.doc: The TechDraw ExtensionLockUnlockView tool locks or unlocks the position of a view by toggling its Lock Position property. A locked view has a fixed position relative to the page or the group it belongs to.

TechDraw_ExtensionPosChainDimensionGroup.doc: Aligns the horizontal dimensions to create a chain dimension:- Select two or more horizontal dimensions- The first dimension defines the position- Click this tool.

TechDraw_ExtensionPosHorizChainDimension.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionPosHorizChainDimension tool aligns horizontal dimensions to create a chain dimension.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionPosVertChainDimension
- TechDraw_ExtensionPosObliqueChainDimension

TechDraw_ExtensionPosObliqueChainDimensi.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionPosObliqueChainDimension tool aligns oblique dimensions to create a chain dimension.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionPosHorizChainDimension
- TechDraw_ExtensionPosVertChainDimension

TechDraw_ExtensionPosVertChainDimension.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionPosVertChainDimension tool aligns vertical dimensions to create a chain dimension.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionPosHorizChainDimension
- TechDraw_ExtensionPosObliqueChainDimension

TechDraw_ExtensionPositionSectionView.doc: The TechDraw ExtensionPositionSectionView tool orthogonally aligns a section view with its source view. You can select a section view or ( ) select an edge and a vertex.

TechDraw_ExtensionRemovePrefixChar.doc: The TechDraw ExtensionRemovePrefixChar tool removes all prefix symbols from the dimension text.

TechDraw_ExtensionSelectLineAttributes.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionSelectLineAttributes tool opens a dialog box where you can select the attributes (style, width and color) for new cosmetic lines and centerlines created with the Extensions tools, and specify the cascade spacing and delta distance. The line attributes are also used by the TechDraw ExtensionChangeLineAttributes tool.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionChangeLineAttributes

TechDraw_ExtensionShortenLine.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionShortenLine tool shortens a cosmetic line or centerline at both ends.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionExtendLine

TechDraw_ExtensionThreadBoltBottom.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionThreadBoltBottom tool adds a cosmetic thread to the top or bottom view of bolts/screws/rods.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionThreadHoleBottom

TechDraw_ExtensionThreadBoltSide.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionThreadBoltSide tool adds a cosmetic thread to the side view of a bolt/screw/rod.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionThreadHoleSide

TechDraw_ExtensionThreadHoleBottom.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionThreadHoleBottom tool adds a cosmetic thread to the top or bottom view of holes.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionThreadBoltBottom

TechDraw_ExtensionThreadHoleSide.doc:
The TechDraw ExtensionThreadHoleSide tool adds a cosmetic thread to the side view of a hole.

## See also

- TechDraw_ExtensionThreadBoltSide

TechDraw_ExtensionThreadsGroup.doc: Add a cosmetic thread to the side view of a selected hole between two selected parallel lines.

TechDraw_ExtensionVertexAtIntersection.doc: The TechDraw ExtensionVertexAtIntersection tool adds cosmetic vertex(es) at the intersection(s) of selected edges.

TechDraw_ExtentGroup.doc: Inserts a dimension showing the extent (overall length) of an object or feature.

TechDraw_FaceCenterLine.doc:
The TechDraw FaceCenterLine tool adds a centerline to selected faces.

## See also

- TechDraw_2LineCenterLine
- TechDraw_2PointCenterLine

TechDraw_FillTemplateFields.doc: The FillTemplateFields tool fills the editable text fields in the title block of the current page.

TechDraw_GeometricHatch.doc:
The TechDraw GeometricHatch tool fills a closed region in a View with a pattern based on an AutoDesk PAT hatching specification. Alternatively the TechDraw Hatch tool uses SVG based hatch patterns. See Hatching for details.

## See also

- TechDraw_Hatch
- TechDraw_Hatching

TechDraw_Hatch.doc:
The TechDraw Hatch tool fills a closed region in a View with a tiled SVG or bitmap ( ) based hatch pattern. Alternatively the TechDraw GeometricHatch tool uses PAT based hatch patterns. See Hatching for details.

## See also

- TechDraw_GeometricHatch
- TechDraw_Hatching

TechDraw_HoleShaftFit.doc:
The TechDraw HoleShaftFit tool adds hole or shaft tolerances using ISO 286 to a linear dimension or a diameter dimension.

## See also

- TechDraw_Geometric_dimensioning_and_tolerancing

TechDraw_HorizontalDimension.doc:
The TechDraw HorizontalDimension tool adds a horizontal dimension to a View. The dimension may be the horizontal distance between two points or the horizontal length of a straight edge. As with the TechDraw LengthDimension tool it is also possible to select two edges or a point and an edge, but these options make less sense for this tool.

For more information see TechDraw LengthDimension.

## See also

- TechDraw_LengthDimension
- TechDraw_VerticalDimension

TechDraw_HorizontalExtentDimension.doc:
The TechDraw HorizontalExtentDimension tool adds a linear dimension to a View. The dimension extends from the left most point on the selected objects to the right most point.

## See also

- TechDraw_LengthDimension
- TechDraw_VerticalExtentDimension

TechDraw_Image.doc:
The TechDraw Image tool inserts a bitmap image (PNG, TIFF, JPEG, etc.) from a file into the page as a view. The TechDraw View tool can also create an Image View.

## See also

- TechDraw_Symbol

TechDraw_LeaderLine.doc:
The TechDraw LeaderLine tool adds a line to a View. Other annotation objects (such as Rich Text Annotations) can be connected to the leaderline to form complex annotations.

## See also

- TechDraw_RichTextAnnotation
- TechDraw_WeldSymbol

TechDraw_LengthDimension.doc:
The TechDraw LengthDimension tool adds a linear dimension to a View. The dimension may be the distance between two points, the length of a straight edge, the perpendicular distance between two edges, or the perpendicular distance between a point and an edge.

## See also

- TechDraw_HorizontalDimension
- TechDraw_VerticalDimension

TechDraw_Midpoints.doc:
The TechDraw Midpoints tool adds cosmetic vertices at the midpoint of one or more selected edges.

## See also

- TechDraw_CosmeticVertex
- TechDraw_Quadrants

TechDraw_MoveView.doc:
The TechDraw MoveView tool moves a View and all its dependents (Balloons, Dimensions, etc) to a different Page.

## See also

- TechDraw_ShareView

TechDraw_PageDefault.doc:
The TechDraw PageDefault tool creates a new Page object using the the template file specified in the TechDraw Preferences.

## See also

- TechDraw_PageTemplate
- TechDraw_Templates

TechDraw_PageTemplate.doc:
The TechDraw PageTemplate tool creates a new Page object using the template file selected from a dialog.

The starting directory for the dialog can be specified in the TechDraw Preferences.

## See also

- TechDraw_PageDefault
- TechDraw_Templates

TechDraw_PrintAll.doc:
The TechDraw PrintAll tool sends all pages in a document to the printer.

## See also

- Std_Print

TechDraw_ProjectShape.doc:
The TechDraw ProjectShape tool creates projections of shapes. The projections are created in the 3D view, and not on a TechDraw Page.

## See also

- Draft_Shape2DView

TechDraw_ProjectionGroup.doc:
The TechDraw ProjectionGroup tool creates a multiview projection of one or more 3D objects, using the traditional first- or third-angle projection. The isometric views of the 4 front corners can also be included. The TechDraw View tool can also create a Projection Group. It is advisable to use that tool instead.

## See also

- TechDraw_View

TechDraw_Quadrants.doc:
The TechDraw Quadrant tool adds three cosmetic vertices along the length of one or more selected edges. The vertices are placed at 25%, 50% and 75% of the length of the edges. For a circular edge this results in cosmetic vertices at 90°, 180° and 270°, in addition to its geometric vertex at 0°.

## See also

- TechDraw_CosmeticVertex
- TechDraw_Midpoints

TechDraw_RadiusDimension.doc:
The TechDraw RadiusDimension tool adds a radius dimension to a View. The dimension may be applied to any edge which is a circle or circular arc.

## See also

- TechDraw_DiameterDimension

TechDraw_RedrawPage.doc: The TechDraw RedrawPage tool forces a page update despite any contrary settings of KeepUpdated (Page property), Update with 3D (parameter) or Allow Page Override (parameter).

TechDraw_RichTextAnnotation.doc:
The TechDraw RichTextAnnotation tool adds a formatted annotation block to a Leaderline or a View.

## See also

- TechDraw_Annotation

TechDraw_SectionGroup.doc: Inserts a simple or complex section view in the current page.

TechDraw_SectionView.doc:
The TechDraw SectionView tool inserts a cross-section view based on an existing part view.

## See also

- TechDraw_ComplexSection
- TechDraw_View

TechDraw_ShareView.doc: The TechDraw ShareView tool makes a View and all its dependents (Balloons, Dimensions, etc) visible on a second Page.

TechDraw_ShowAll.doc:
The TechDraw ShowAll tool is intended to temporarily show, and then hide, invisible lines in a View. Lines can be made invisible with the TechDraw DecorateLine tool. Note that "invisible" is a cosmetic state, not to be confused with hidden lines which are geometric constructs.

## See also

- TechDraw_DecorateLine

TechDraw_SpreadsheetView.doc: The TechDraw SpreadsheetView tool allows you to place a view of a selected spreadsheet on a Page. The TechDraw View tool can also create a Spreadsheet View.

TechDraw_StackBottom.doc:
The TechDraw StackBottom tool moves Views to the bottom of the stacking order. The stacking order controls the apparent depth of Views on a page.

See TechDraw StackTop.

## See also

- TechDraw_StackTop
- TechDraw_StackUp
- TechDraw_StackDown

TechDraw_StackDown.doc:
The TechDraw StackDown tool moves Views down one level in the stacking order. The stacking order controls the apparent depth of Views on a page.

See TechDraw StackTop.

## See also

- TechDraw_StackTop
- TechDraw_StackBottom
- TechDraw_StackUp

TechDraw_StackGroup.doc: Adjusts the stacking order of the selected views.

TechDraw_StackTop.doc:
The TechDraw StackTop tool moves Views to the top of the stacking order. The stacking order controls the apparent depth of Views on a page.

## See also

- TechDraw_StackBottom
- TechDraw_StackUp
- TechDraw_StackDown.

TechDraw_StackUp.doc:
The TechDraw StackUp tool moves Views up one level in the stacking order. The stacking order controls the apparent depth of Views on a page.

See TechDraw StackTop.

## See also

- TechDraw_StackTop
- TechDraw_StackBottom
- TechDraw_StackDown

TechDraw_SurfaceFinishSymbols.doc: The TechDraw SurfaceFinishSymbols tool adds a surface finish symbol to a page.

TechDraw_Symbol.doc:
The TechDraw Symbol tool inserts a Symbol object. A Symbol is a stripped down view that contains only a single SVG file complying with the svg-tiny specification (see TechDraw Templates).

A Symbol can be anything that helps annotate a drawing and that doesn't need to be further modified, it may however contain editable texts. The TechDraw View tool can also create a Symbol.

## See also

- TechDraw_Templates
- Draft_SVG

TechDraw_ToggleFrame.doc:
The TechDraw ToggleFrame tool turns the display of View frames, labels and vertices on or off.

## See also

- TechDraw_View

TechDraw_VerticalDimension.doc:
The TechDraw VerticalDimension tool adds a vertical dimension to a View. The dimension may be the vertical distance between two points or the vertical length of a straight edge. As with the TechDraw LengthDimension tool it is also possible to select two edges or a point and an edge, but these options make less sense for this tool.

For more information see TechDraw LengthDimension.

## See also

- TechDraw_LengthDimension
- TechDraw_HorizontalDimension

TechDraw_VerticalExtentDimension.doc:
The TechDraw VerticalExtentDimension tool adds a linear dimension to a View. The dimension extends from the bottom most point on the selected objects to the top most point.

For more information see TechDraw HorizontalExtentDimension.

## See also

- TechDraw_LengthDimension
- TechDraw_HorizontalExtentDimension

TechDraw_View.doc:
The TechDraw View tool adds a representation of one or more objects to a Drawing page. It can create a Projection Group Item (a single view), a Projection Group, a Spreadsheet View, an Arch View, a Symbol or an Image View.

In the tool can only create a Part View, which is very similar to a Projection Group Item.

## See also

- TechDraw_ProjectionGroup
- TechDraw_SpreadsheetView
- TechDraw_ArchView
- TechDraw_Symbol
- TechDraw_Image

TechDraw_WeldSymbol.doc:
The TechDraw WeldingSymbol tool adds welding specifications to an existing leader line.

## See also

- TechDraw_LeaderLine

Test_TestBaseText.doc: Test the basic functions of FreeCAD.

Test_TestDeleteMenu.doc: Test the menu stuff of FreeCAD.

Test_TestDocText.doc: Test the document (creation, save, load and destruction).
